gcTMB: Fitting Growth Curves Using the Template Model Builder

Source: R/gcTMB-package.R
gcTMB-package.Rd

Fits non-linear growth curves over time by maximum likelihood using the Template Model Builder ('TMB'), with covariates on the parameters and random effects, which are integrated out by the Laplace approximation, and autocorrelated residuals. The main function gcTMB() fits the logistic (Richards), Gompertz, Hill, Weibull, normal and gamma growth curves, each with an asymmetry parameter, the Chapman-Richards and Korf curves with an intercept, e.g. for height-diameter models, the beta growth function, capped at its maximum or not, the Preece-Baines model of human growth, and a straight line for comparison. The curves are parameterised by the asymptote (or, with b1type = "rate", the maximum growth rate), a time (of the maximum growth rate or of half the asymptote), a scale, slope or shape parameter, a threshold time before which a truncated curve is zero, and the asymmetry, each with an identity, log, logit or inverse link, and any of them can be fixed. The response can follow a Gaussian, lognormal, Poisson, binomial, beta-binomial, beta or negative binomial (nbinom1, nbinom2) distribution, with case weights. Fixed effects are formulas for each parameter, e.g. b1 + b2 ~ treatment, and random effects are written as in 'nlme', e.g. b1 + b2 ~ 1 | individual: they can be correlated across the parameters, with several terms, nested or crossed grouping factors and random slopes. The Gaussian and lognormal residuals can be autocorrelated within individuals, with the first-order autoregressive structures corAR1() and continuous-time corCAR1() of 'nlme', or the exponential corExp() and Gaussian corGaus() with an optional nugget, whose objects are accepted as well. Starting values are found by a linearisation of the curves or a grid search (gcTMBstart()), and the optimisation is controlled by gcTMBcontrol(). Inference covers Wald, profile likelihood and parametric bootstrap confidence intervals (confint(), profile(), bootstrap()), small-sample t and F inference for Gaussian and lognormal models without random effects, likelihood ratio tests with chi-square, F or parametric bootstrap p-values (anova()), information criteria such as AIC, AICc, BIC and HQIC and goodness-of-fit criteria (criteria()), and tests of the differences of a parameter between curves, against a reference or between all pairs, with multiplicity adjustment (partest()). The times at which the curves reach a percentage of their asymptote or a given response (timeto()), and the maximum growth rates, their timing and the fraction of the asymptote reached then (maxrate()), are derived with standard errors by automatic differentiation and the delta method, and with profile likelihood and bootstrap intervals, for the population curves, and for timeto() also for fitted individuals. Methods for gcTMB fits include summary(), predict() with confidence and prediction intervals of the curves or their parameters, fitted() and residuals() (Pearson, randomised quantile and normalized), plot() of validation plots and fitted curves, viewcurves() to step through the observed curves of the individuals of any data set in a 'shiny' app, simulate() at the observed or new times and individuals, update() to refit the model or set its parameters as the true model of a simulation study, logLik(), coef(), vcov(), converged(), and the extractors fixef(), ranef(), VarCorr(), sigma() and corpars(), compatible with 'nlme' and 'lme4'. The data sets FabaHeights25 (heights of faba bean plants under five treatments) and FabaCounts23 (pod counts of six faba bean genotypes) illustrate the methods. Four vignettes cover the growth models and their parameters, fixed and random effects, the timing and maximum growth rates, and autocorrelation and simulation, and an overview shows most of the features in one document.

Growth models and fitting

gcTMB fits the growth curves: logistic (Richards), Gompertz, Hill, Weibull, normal and gamma, each with an asymmetry b5, the Chapman-Richards, beta and Korf curves, and a straight line. The parameters are the asymptote b1 (or the maximum growth rate, b1type="rate"), the time b2 of the maximum growth rate or of half the asymptote, the scale, slope or shape b3, the threshold b4 of a truncated curve and the asymmetry b5, each with a link and optionally fixed; the Chapman-Richards and Korf height-diameter models keep the parameters usual in forestry (see gcTMB). gcTMBstart gives the starting values and gcTMBcontrol the settings of the optimisation and the inference.

Effects, distributions and autocorrelation

Fixed effects of covariates on the parameters (fform) and random effects (rform), correlated across parameters, with several terms, nested or crossed factors and random slopes; the families gaussian, lognormal, poisson, binomial, betabinomial, beta, nbinom1 and nbinom2; and autocorrelated residuals within individuals, corAR1, corCAR1, corExp and corGaus (with a nugget for measurement error).

Inference

  • summary.gcTMB, coef, vcov, logLik, converged;

  • confidence intervals: confint.gcTMB (profile likelihood, Wald, bootstrap), profile.gcTMB, bootstrap;

  • tests and model choice: anova.gcTMB (likelihood ratio, F and parametric bootstrap tests), criteria (information and goodness-of-fit criteria), partest (tests of the differences between curves: each curve against a reference, Dunnett, or all pairs, Tukey, with single-step adjustment).

Timing and growth rates

timeto, the times to reach a percentage of the asymptote or a given response, and maxrate, the maximum growth rate, its timing and the fraction of the asymptote reached then, with standard errors and confint and profile methods.

Predictions, diagnostics and simulation

predict.gcTMB (curves and parameters, with confidence and prediction intervals), fitted, residuals.gcTMB (Pearson, randomised quantile, normalized), plot.gcTMB (validation plots and curves), viewcurves (a shiny app to step through the observed curves of the individuals of any data set), simulate.gcTMB (at the observed or new times and individuals), and update.gcTMB (refit, or set the parameters of a true model for simulation).

Extractors

fixef, ranef, VarCorr, sigma, corpars and varpars, compatible with nlme and lme4 (see gcTMB, Relation to nlme).

Data and vignettes

The data sets FabaHeights25 and FabaCounts23. The vignettes: vignette("gcTMB"), an overview of most features; vignette("growth-models"), vignette("fixed-random-effects"), vignette("timing-rates"), vignette("correlation"), vignette("variance") and vignette("simulation").
